items.stem: A mobile app disables TLS certificate validation 'to make development easier' and ships that way. Why is this dangerous?

options.text: It lets an attacker intercept and alter traffic via a man-in-the-middle, defeating HTTPS protection
options.rationale: Correct: without certificate validation the client will trust an attacker's certificate, exposing all traffic.

options.text: It only slows the app down slightly
options.rationale: The issue is a serious confidentiality and integrity breach, not speed.

options.text: It improves security by skipping checks
options.rationale: Skipping validation removes protection; it does not improve security.

options.text: It has no effect because HTTPS is used
options.rationale: HTTPS with disabled validation provides no real protection.

items.explanation: Correct: without certificate validation the client will trust an attacker's certificate, exposing all traffic.

items.stem: Which TWO are sound practices for storing sensitive data on a mobile device? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Store secrets in the platform keystore or keychain rather than plain files
options.rationale: Correct: platform secure storage is designed to protect keys and secrets.

options.text: Avoid logging tokens or credentials to disk
options.rationale: Correct: tokens written to logs or disk can be read by other processes or attackers.

options.text: Hard-code an API secret in the app binary
options.rationale: Secrets in the binary can be extracted by reverse engineering.

options.text: Save passwords in plain text for convenience

items.explanation: Correct: platform secure storage is designed to protect keys and secrets.

items.stem: A team relies on client-side obfuscation to keep an embedded API key secret. What is the correct understanding?

options.text: Obfuscation raises the effort but cannot keep a client-side secret truly secret; secrets belong server-side
options.rationale: Correct: anything shipped to the client can be extracted; real secrets must stay on the server.

options.text: Obfuscation makes the key mathematically impossible to recover
options.rationale: Obfuscation only delays analysis; it does not make recovery impossible.

options.text: A client-side key is as safe as a server-side one
options.rationale: Client-side secrets are inherently exposed, unlike server-side ones.

options.text: Obfuscation removes the need for server authorisation
options.rationale: Server-side authorisation is still required regardless of obfuscation.

items.explanation: Correct: anything shipped to the client can be extracted; real secrets must stay on the server.
